Chapter 17 of 19

The Eternal Night

Deep NightDTES160 BPM
The story

Morning does not destroy the darkness. It only moves it. All the night that the city cannot use in daylight has to be stored somewhere, and it is stored in the Eternal Night: inside old brick, hotel windows, alley mouths, awnings, loading doors, stairwells and the deepest architectural shadows of the Downtown Eastside.

Lost minutes are kept there too. The district is not dark because of the people who live in it. Its buildings are simply carrying more night than the rest of the city, and while the rest of the city sleeps, its hidden systems keep working: culture, machinery, animals, the slow business of the deep hours.

The Repair People mark the spots where darkness leaks out. The Wire Choir sounds lower and slower here. And if you ever find a clock in the Eternal Night, do not use it. Light goes in. Night stays. Time missing. Store it here.

Terminal City is an original fictional mythology inspired by Vancouver’s geography, weather, wildlife, infrastructure, art, and electronic music. It makes no claim to historical, Indigenous, or religious tradition. Real places are used as settings; the operating system layered on them is invented. Photograph reality. Alter the evidence. Never illustrate the whole myth.
